chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Fadhdhal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said:
'Eat from the birds what had a gizzard, or a spur, or a crop (craw).'

key_terms.حَوْصَلَةٌ: crop (craw) — a pouch in the throat of birds where food is stored before digestion
key_terms.صِيصِيَةٌ: spur — a sharp projection on the leg of certain birds, especially roosters and game birds
key_terms.قَانِصَةٌ: gizzard — the muscular stomach found in grain-eating birds, used to grind food

ai.seo_question: How can you tell if a bird is permissible (halal) to eat in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a practical jurisprudential rule for identifying permissible birds: any bird possessing a gizzard, a spur, or a crop may be eaten. This ruling provides three anatomical signs that serve as indicators of permissibility in the absence of explicit Quranic designation. In classical Shia fiqh, these bodily features were understood to distinguish grain-eating birds (generally halal) from birds of prey (generally haram), enabling Muslims to determine permissibility based on observable physical characteristics.
